requirements.requirement: Publishing a valid release atomically updates current so concurrent readers continuously see a complete previous or new release.
requirements.summary: The repaired publisher creates a replacement symlink and renames it over current in the same directory. A bounded test performed 200 alternating publications while 789 concurrent reads found current continuously resolvable and observed only coherent release-one or release-two content. Explicit publication and rollback also succeeded after restart.

requirements.requirement: A release missing MANIFEST is refused without changing the existing current target.
requirements.summary: The incomplete release was rejected with exit status 1, while the current target and served content remained release one. The same rejection behavior was directly verified after restart.

requirements.requirement: Both staged releases remain intact and rollback to either release remains possible.
requirements.summary: Publication to release two and rollback to release one were demonstrated before and after restart. Checksums for both staged releases match the preparation baseline, and the final directory inventory retains releases one and two.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 remained unchanged. The POSIX-shell publisher passed syntax checks and functioned before and after reboot using utilities available on the installed platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Atomic reader behavior, rejection safety, forward publication, rollback, staged-release preservation, platform preservation, and post-restart recovery were directly demonstrated. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle observations, and recovered publisher behavior and data.
limitations: Atomic continuity was demonstrated through a strong bounded stress test (200 transitions and 789 reads), but finite testing cannot exhaust every possible scheduler interleaving.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The publisher edit and temporary backup supported the repair; publication/rejection tests and temporary files were bounded evidence collection; the backup and test artifacts were removed; and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. Final observations show no failed services, no new network exposure, and healthy package state. Socket and systemd-private-file differences are normal consequences of the verified reboot.
